title: Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress
summary: Two new graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress have arrived within weeks of each other. Here's how they are similar and different, and my recommendation of which one to buy. See Also A La Carte (July 27) The Puritans: John Bunyan A La Carte (6/3)
content: I have often expressed how spoiled Christian readers are today. As if we needed more proof of this, how about the fact that in a single month, publishers released not one but two major graphic novel adaptations of Pilgrim’s Progress ? Both are well-written, beautifully illustrated, and faithful to Bunyan’s story. Let me help you understand their similarities and differences and tell you which one might be best to add to your library. Christian’s Quest is written by Tyler Van Halteren and illustrated by Manuel Zepic. It is published by Lithos Kids, which has already released the three-part Little Pilgrim’s Big Journey , an illustrated adaptation of Pilgrim’s Progress for young readers, and The Mansoul Chronicles , which is based on Bunyan’s Holy War . It is a 220-page 7×10.63 inch hardcover that targets children aged 8+, though it is meant to be enjoyed by teens and adults as well. Its illustrations are what I might describe as a clean, polished YA style. The lines are thin and tidy and much of the form comes from shading. The colors tend to maintain a soft, muted, painted look. It lightly updates some antiquated language so that Bunyan’s Slough of Despond becomes the Bog of Despond. Christian is youthful and fresh-faced, and his burden is a bulging pack on a frame. It includes some bonus material: a behind-the-scenes look at how a graphic novel is made, and a study guide that explains and applies each of the stages of Christian’s quest. It also indicates that a sequel, Christiana’s Crown , will be released in 2028. Pilgrim’s Progress: The Graphic Novel is written by Jeremy Patenaude, illustrated by Brent McKee, colored by Matt Wilson, and lettered by Taylor Esposito. It is published by Crossway as what I believe is the company’s first graphic novel, though it has a long history of publishing books for young readers. It is a 256-page 7×10.25 inch paperback that targets readers aged 14+. Its illustrations are what I might describe as gritty and stylized and perhaps a bit more indie than mainstream. It uses heavy brush ink, dark shadows, and vivid colors. It does not update Bunyan’s antiquated language. Christian is a gaunt, tormented, weathered adult whose burden is a huge stone roped to his back. Its bonus material includes a lexicon of the key characters and locations and reflections on each of the chapters. There is no indication of a sequel that will cover Christiana’s quest. While these two graphic novels tell the same story and tell it faithfully using dialogue and illustration rather than narration, they tell it using different visual language largely because Christian’s Quest is meant to be accessible to a younger demographic. You might say that Christian’s Quest is a bit more kid-friendly and Pilgrim’s Progress is a bit more adult-friendly, though both could easily be enjoyed by kids and adults alike. After all, who doesn’t enjoy reading the occasional graphic novel? Another key difference is that Pilgrim’s Progress is a paperback where Christian’s Quest is being sold as more of an heirloom object that features cloth binding, gold foil, and a ribbon marker. Let me show you a few examples of the art from each book. Christian’s Quest These are drawn from the publisher’s preview images. Pilgrim’s Progress These are drawn from the sample chapter on Crossway’s site. My Recommendation Which do I recommend? Either! Both! If your readers are younger, Christian’s Quest is the more obvious choice, and if they are older—teenagers and up—they may prefer Pilgrim’s Progress . But you couldn’t go wrong with either, and you couldn’t go wrong with picking up both. title: A La Carte (November 12)
summary: On spouses sitting together in church / Can’t you just be like me? / Husbands, pray for your wives / Six comforts for pastors / The most fun I ever had / Will we really be perfect in heaven? / The most offensive doctrine / Kindle deals and more See Also A La Carte (October 7) A La Carte (September 3) A La Carte (August 1)
content: I hope you don’t mind that this is a bit of a book-heavy week, but I’ve had a lot of book content I have wanted to share. Hence, we’ve had This Week in Christian Books , The First 100 Books for the Children’s Section of Your Church Library , and Spoiled for Choice: Two New Graphic Novels of Pilgrim’s Progress . A book review will follow tomorrow, then we’ll be mostly caught up for now. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include P rioritizing the Church in Missions , Growing Up , and several good books for children. Recommended Reading On Spouses Sitting Together in Church. I happened to spot some of the kerfuffle that erupted after TGC Australia shared an article about why spouses should consider not sitting together in church. As happens on social media, the response seemed far out of proportion to the article. I found Murray Campbell’s response a good and reasonable one, even if I intend to keep sitting with Aileen most Sundays. Can’t You Just Be Like Me? I suppose in some ways, Bobby Scott’s piece on tribalism and disunity could nicely follow the previous article. “Tribalistic churches and Christians demand conformity to their broad range of preferences, believing they are inviolable God-ordained principles. So they strive to silence or coerce other Christians to assimilate, or they quietly despise these brothers and sisters. This inevitably leads to dark consequences. Instead of loving other Christians who have the same primary biblical convictions but differ over tertiary issues, tribalistic Christians feel justified in waging war against them.” Nelson’s Complete Book of Bible Maps and Charts is out in a fourth edition, updated with new high-resolution photography to go with its full-color maps, timelines, and charts for every book of the Bible. (Sponsored) Husbands, Pray for Your Wives. Costi Hinn: “I’ll never forget the first time I sat in a men’s Bible study on a Saturday morning listening to a man unpack the importance of praying for your wife. I was honestly blown away by the simplicity of it all and how I had never thought to pray for her — and I mean, like really pray for her.” He outlines eight ways men can do so. Six Comforts for Pastors. This article from Darryl Dash delivers what it promises. “If we base our identity on how well our ministries are going from an earthly perspective, we will be in trouble. Every pastor’s ministry will have good times and bad times. Basing our identity on how well things seem to be going is like putting our hope in a volatile stock. We will end up elated some of the time and despondent the rest. As pastors, we need to put our confidence in something more secure than how well things seem to be going. Here are six comforts for pastors that will last and sustain us, no matter how well or poorly our ministry seems to be going.” The Most Fun I Ever Had. Concerned about all those who are disparaging motherhood today, Brittany Allen chooses to celebrate it. “I still find it hard to write articles about the joys of motherhood because I never want to isolate sisters who are longing for a family. Yet, at the same time, I want to talk back to our culture that treats motherhood as a curse rather than a gift.” Will We Really Be Perfect in Heaven? Randy Alcorn: “Someone e-mailed me this question: ‘In Heaven, will some people still be annoying? After all, eternity’s a long time!’ Annoyance is sometimes caused by others’ sin, our own, or both. Since sin will be eliminated, so will annoyance. That doesn’t mean people won’t have idiosyncrasies, only that they won’t be rooted in sin, and none of us will degrade or dismiss others.” He explains what it means that we will be perfect in heaven. The Most Offensive Doctrine Every now and again, I like to share a quote that I have encountered through my reading. This is drawn from J.C. Ryle’s Expository Thoughts on Luke , which I’m enjoying a lot. Of all the doctrines of the Bible, none is so offensive to human nature as the doctrine of God’s sovereignty.

summary: A new serpent in the garden of Africa / On naming the dead / Why your favorite worship song’s grammar matters / 3 Reasons you should not date while watching porn / Would you forgive me of my narcissism? / Christianity Today and the sin of centrism / Kindle deals, videos, and more See Also A La Carte (June 27) Weekend A La Carte (October 25) Kindle Deals for Christian Readers
content: Good morning, my friends. The God of love and peace be with you today. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include Paul Tripp & Timothy Lane’s excellent Relationships: A Mess Worth Making , R.C. Sproul’s Growing in Holiness (which I don’t think I’ve seen on sale before), and Jonathan Landry Cruse’s What Happens When We Worship , among others. If you’d like to celebrate Advent with Spurgeon, Westminster Books has a deal on a new devotional book that may be of interest to you. If that’s not quite right for you, there’s lots of other resources in the Advent Sale . Recommended Reading A New Serpent in the Garden of Africa. “Just as the serpent led Adam and Eve into idolatry by reinterpreting God’s good word, so prosperity and word-of-faith preachers are today proclaiming a false and idolatrous gospel. But unlike Adam, African preachers are refusing to stay mute. Recognizing the need for faithful interpretation of Scripture, they have drawn up a statement to help pastors stand against the idolatrous assumptions and teachings of the prosperity gospel and word-of-faith theology.” Dieudonné Tamfu writes from an African perspective and describes the importance of the recent Africa Statement on the Prosperity Gospel and Word of Faith Theology . On Naming the Dead. Andrew Roycroft explains why it’s important that we not merely remember the dead, but name them. “The park bench copperplate, the trinkets and human ephemera that we treasure more than diamonds, the ongoing dedication of certain pieces of music truly matter, and keep back the dimming power of death for a time. Recently, in the wake of my friend’s death, I have been seeking to honour him by reading his favourite authors, enjoying afresh what I know he enjoyed and feeling a continued sense of fraternity and fellowship through these authors who meant so much to him.” Why Your Favorite Worship Song’s Grammar Matters. Porter C. Taylor explains why grammar matters when it comes to worship songs, and why the Psalms model the kind of worship that serves us best. “What if the worship wars have been fighting the wrong battle? What if contemporary worship music supplies a necessary register too often missing from our musical praise before our Creator? The question we should ask of our worship songs is not simply whether they make accurate statements about God. We should also ask what they enable the gathered church to say and do before God.” Nelson’s Complete Book of Bible Maps and Charts is out in a fourth edition, updated with new high-resolution photography to go with its full-color maps, timelines, and charts for every book of the Bible.  (Sponsored) 3 Reasons You Should Not Date While Watching Porn. I don’t think I am the only one who has been asked this question many times over: Should I refrain from dating until I am free from porn? Jacob Valk answers in the affirmative and offers three good reasons. Would You Forgive Me of My Narcissism? John Beeson explains why narcissism may not just be a problem that others have. “The most discussed personality disorder of our day is narcissism. A brief foray into Google Trends (always a fun rabbit hole to go down) shows that through the early 2000s, narcissism was searched about as often as some of the more well-known personality disorders. In 2015, that number began to rise and by 2022, it rocketed way above any other psychiatric disorder search. That aligns with my own experience as it is now a regular occurrence for me to hear a counselee accuse someone else of narcissism.” Christianity Today and the Sin of Centrism. content: Tuesday is the day most publishers release their new books, so each week I like to let you know what has just come our way from the publishers I follow most closely. It is a quieter week than the last one, but it brings a revised edition of B. B. Warfield’s Biblical and Theological Studies, Alex Duke’s guided tour of Exodus (for which I provided a foreword), and two Crossway editions marking 500 years since William Tyndale’s English New Testament. On the academic side, you’ll find several noteworthy titles, including the New International Commentary on the Old Testament volume on Daniel 7–12. In each case, I’ve included the publisher’s description. Books for Everyone Zondervan From Silence to Sinai A Guided Tour of Exodus Alex Duke Publisher’s description What adjectives would you use to describe the Bible? Inspired. Amazing. Unique. Authoritative. Perfect. Pure. Life-changing. Those descriptions are all deserved. Your pastors and parents and Sunday School teachers were right. There’s no book like God’s Book. Here’s another adjective: confusing. The Bible can be confusing, especially certain parts of the Old Testament. Moments after coming across something inspiring and encouraging, you’ll read something that makes you wonder, What is even happening right now!? The book of Exodus is no exception. This sequel to Genesis begins with God’s surprising silence. What a stark contrast to Genesis, where God’s words set everything in motion. It then tells the story of God’s miraculous liberation of his people, complete with frogs falling from the sky and life-saving blood being painted over doorways. Finally, for the last half of the book, the action slows down as the people of God gather at the mountain of God to receive the Law of God in order to engage in the worship of God. From silence to Sinai, that’s the story of Exodus. To understand it all, most of us will need a guide. We’ll need some help. That’s what From Silence to Sinai is for. Alex Duke walks readers through the book of Exodus to show that nothing in God’s story is wasted—not the silence, not the ten signs, and not even the confusing parts. In Exodus, God is not absent, random, or unclear. He is revealing himself, redeeming his people, and teaching them how to live in his presence. Buy it at Amazon or Westminster Books . B&H The First Five Beating the Odds and Thriving as a Ministry Leader Kyle Worley and Joseph Worley Publisher’s description Is it possible to do more than survive in ministry leadership? Could you actually thrive? The alarming reality is that most ministry leaders will not make it more than five years in leadership. Burnout, lack of training, and an absence of coaches are all pitfalls on the road to sustainable ministry leadership. But there is a different roadmap for those willing to learn. In The First Five , Joseph and Kyle Worley present a pathway for thriving in ministry leadership. With over sixty years of experience, across churches of every size and shape, they provide a biblically rooted and tested approach to the personal, professional, and pastoral dynamics of ministry leadership. The First Five is designed to be a manual for new ministry leaders and those leading them. Don’t just read this book—use it! You can do more than survive as a ministry leader. We believe you can thrive. Buy it at Amazon . Preorder · releases Wednesday, November 11 P&R Biblical and Theological Studies Revised and Enhanced Benjamin B. Warfield, edited by John J. content: Let me take a moment to remind you of some of the features of this site you may not know about. I have a growing page of Liturgies meant to help the local church in its worship. I also offer Book Recommendations across many categories and a list of the Best Commentaries for each book of the Bible. And if you like the quote graphics I share day by day, you can find them all at SquareQuotes.church where they are free to download. Sales & Deals Today’s Kindle deals include several of the “Heart Talks” mini books that are meant to help women with common concerns: feeling like failures in parenting, husbands who lead poorly, doubt, and so on. You’ll also find Greg Gifford’s Lies My Therapist Told Me and several other titles. Recommended Reading Beer, Beef and Player’s Navy Cut. This is a brilliant article about C.S. Lewis and the vices that dogged him throughout his life—a three-pack-a day smoking habit, eating habits that bordered on gluttony, and far more alcohol than anyone should consume. “In case you really are new here and you mostly know Lewis from the kid’s books, let’s state the obvious: the man we universally honor as one of the 20th Century’s great saints smoked, ate and drank like he was a sponsored athlete of consumption. He sinned frequently through overindulgence. What do we do with this information?” How to Graciously Say No. You have probably run into the same conclusion I have: it’s often far harder to say no than to say yes. Yet sometimes the best thing we can do for ourselves and for others is to say no. Reagan Rose offers some thoughts on that (for those who have the ability to say no, of course, since in many occupations saying no isn’t an option). Can’t You Let Me Just Attend? “We live in a chronically noncommittal society. No wonder, then, that this has been dubbed the age of anxiety. Surely, covenant relationships aren’t the only cure, but it might surprise us how much stability of soul comes from deep, reliable, unflighty fellowship.” David Mathis explains why commitment to a particular church is so important, even if it’s extremely countercultural. When Morningness Is Confused With Godliness. I always enjoy an article that provides an alternate view of something we almost take for granted. That’s the case with this one from Cole Mizel, who is concerned that we may be too quick to imply that the best Christians do their daily devotions in the morning. “But is it really more virtuous to be a morning person than a night owl?” Everyone Doesn’t React the Same Way. J.V. Fesko makes a simple but wise point here: everyone doesn’t respond to preaching the same way. Because that’s the case, we should not assume that those who display a lot of emotion are necessarily being impacted more than those who do not. “Tears are not the sacrament of a changed heart, the visible sign and seal of an anguished and healed soul.” Evangelising With a Dog. I enjoyed reading Peter Barnes’s account of evangelizing with a dog. “My doctor, who is half my size, suggested as tactfully as he could, what was obvious to all – that my squash days were over, and that I should take to walking the dog in the morning and at lunchtime. So this has become my nod to the need for daily exercise. Being one of the few beings on the planet who still buys a hard copy of a daily newspaper, I take my hound – a cocker spaniel with unusually short legs – with me of a morning. On the way, on most days at least, we pass a stand where two, sometimes three, Jehovah’s Witness ladies seek to engage people in conversation.” New Book Releases New Christian books tend to release on Tuesdays. title: Why Many Profess Christ but Don’t Possess Christ—and What It Means for Discipleship
summary: The gospel still changes everything. But have we embraced something less? The reason many profess Christ but don't possess Christ, and how a reduced understanding of the gospel can leave people mistaking religious activity for saving faith. See Also The Hard Work Is Done—Family Bible Study Is Fun Free-stuff Fridays (Truth78) Evangelize 2024: Growing a Church That Proclaims The Gospel
content: This week, the blog is sponsored by Moody Publishers and adapted from The Unstoppable Gospel by Karl Clauson. It’s impossible to disciple lost people. That sounds obvious. Maybe too obvious to even say out loud. But when the church dilutes or neglects the good news, devastation is left in its wake. After forty years of ministry, this is the most sobering truth I’ve learned about the Western church: We do not merely have a discipleship problem today. We have a gospel problem. Before we ever became weak at disciple-making, we began redefining conversion itself. We slowly traded supernatural regeneration for human decision. Salvation became a prayer to repeat, a card to sign, an aisle to walk, while millions were assured of heaven without ever being transformed by the power of God. We didn’t offer them a belief lacking power, we offered them a powerless belief. The result is a generation that has been deeply Christianized but not necessarily changed. They know the language. They know the songs. They know when to stand, when to sit, when to say amen. They have been immersed in church culture, yet many have never been brought from death to life. We have filled churches with people who have learned how to function in and around “Christianity” without ever truly following Christ. And when that happens, discipleship collapses under the weight of human effort. When evangelism centers on human decision, discipleship inevitably becomes self-powered. Following Jesus is reduced to behavior management, moral striving, and “try harder next time.” The supernatural life Christ promised is replaced with self-help dressed up in religious garb. Dallas Willard spoke of “the Great Omission,” the church’s failure to make disciples. He was right. But I believe something even deeper has happened. Before we omitted discipleship, we compromised the very gospel that births disciples in the first place. That is the crisis. That is the great deception. And until we recover the true faith that changes everything, we will continue trying to disciple people who have never truly been made alive. We have, sitting in our church chairs and pews every weekend—even in good, Bible-teaching churches—vast numbers of people who believe themselves to be saved but possess no power beyond their own efforts and whose lives show only surface evidence of new birth. People assume what they have is all God has for them, not knowing they are cultural Christians, so close yet so far from God. People who have been taught a version of Christianity divorced from repentance, from surrender, from the cost of discipleship and, tragically, from the power that makes the gospel unstoppable. Many profess Christ but don’t possess Christ. We’ve left people needing more, wanting more, and settling for too little. The great deception must end. There is life for the spiritually dead. There is surrender that leads to life instead of loss. There is repentance that produces the rhythm of a flourishing soul. There is discipline that flows from grace instead of fear or performance. And there is deep, liberating, unmistakable freedom when Christ becomes everything. This is why truth must be championed. Not as an idea, but as a reality that cuts, clarifies, and calls us forward. Because when truth becomes really clear, it doesn’t just inform you. It changes you. It brings you out of the fog, out of the confusion, out of the illusion—and into a life that is grounded, whole, and fully alive with God. This is the gospel that birthed the early church. This is the gospel that turned the world upside down. This is the gospel that sustains God’s kids under brutal persecution today. This is the gospel the church has forgotten and the good news it desperately needs. This is the gospel that still changes everything today. Learn more about how we’ve embraced a version of the gospel that falls short of the life Jesus promised, and how you can go from powerless belief to a true faith that changes everything. Get
author: Tim Challies

title: Arrested at the hospital where he worked, he turned the prison into a pulpit
summary: 🇪🇷Eritrea· 2010s
content: Dr Berhane was a new believer in Jesus, working in a hospital in Eritrea, when the secret police came for him. His crime was his faith. They put him in prison for eleven months, in one of the harshest systems on earth, a place designed to make Christians disappear and go quiet. He did the opposite. "Every day I was clapping my hands," he said, "and prisoners would come forward and I shared the gospel." A man who had only recently met Jesus decided his cell was simply the next place to introduce Him. Three Bibles and a valley of death The authorities took his Bible. He smuggled another in. They took that one too, and he smuggled a third. He leaned hard on the Psalms, and when fellow prisoners were taken out and executed, the old line about walking through the valley of the shadow of death stopped being poetry and became the thing that held him upright. Eleven months of that did not break him. It made him a preacher. The guards meant to silence a new Christian and instead handed him a congregation with nowhere to go. Wherever they put you, Jesus goes with you, and He is not intimidated by the walls. Dr Berhane found that out in an Eritrean prison. You can trust it wherever you are.

title: A construction engineer in Madagascar became convinced the Bible was true
summary: 🇲🇬Madagascar· 2013
content: Melias was building things for a living in Madagascar, a construction engineer with a steady trade and, by his own account, no particular expectation that God would interrupt him. In 2013, at twenty-one, God did. It was not dramatic thunder. It was quieter and harder to argue with. "The Holy Spirit convinced my heart that the Bible is true," Melias said. "I found new joy and excitement learning about Jesus through the Scriptures." The book he might have dismissed became the most alive thing in his life. From building houses to building the church He could have kept his new faith as a private comfort and gone on with engineering. Instead he gave it everything. In 2015 he trained for six months as a missionary, and since then he has planted churches and discipled new believers among the Tanala people in Ikongo and the Sakalava in Nosy Be, some of the least reached corners of the island. Now he is training three more Malagasy missionaries to do the same. Madagascar is not a footnote in what God is doing. He is raising up local people like Melias, engineers and tradesmen and ordinary workers, and sending them to their own unreached neighbours. When the Holy Spirit convinces your heart that this is all true, it does not stay a hobby. It becomes the thing you build your life around. He is ready to convince yours.

title: A New Testament sat in his welding workshop until a teenager finally read it
summary: 🇳🇪Agadez· 2000s
content: Someone left a New Testament in Pierre's welding workshop in Niger, and for a while it just sat there. He was a teenager, and eventually he picked it up. What he read did not match what he had been told about Christians. It was full of tenderness, of nearness to the poorest, exactly the kind of world his young heart had been quietly hoping was real. Years later he moved to Agadez, out toward the desert, and there he found the thing the book had described. A church family drawn from Benin, Togo, Burkina Faso, France, and Niger, living out what he had only read about. No regret, not for a single day Pierre became a lay missionary, and he does not hedge when he talks about it. "I have never regretted converting to the Christian faith," he says, "not even for a single day." That is a bold thing to say in Niger, where jihadist groups make following Jesus dangerous and his own children have stayed Muslim, something he carries with love and without pressure. Still, no regret. Not one day. He read about a God who is tender toward the poor, and he found that God to be exactly as advertised. Whatever you have heard about Jesus secondhand, He holds up when you finally meet Him yourself. Pierre would tell you to open the book and see.

title: He was taught Christians do not pray. Then he watched his uncle pray before a meal
content: Charles Yabaga Diarra grew up in a strict Muslim family in Lere, Mali, where Christians were mocked and misunderstood. His father, a headmaster and politician, ran the house like a school. As a boy, Charles fled about a hundred and fifty miles to stay with an uncle, and there he ran straight into something he had been told did not exist. His uncle, a Christian pastor, bowed his head and prayed before the meal. Charles was stunned. "Because we are Christians, we pray before meals," the uncle explained. Charles had been taught that Christians do not pray at all. That simple prayer, in his own language, lodged in him and would not leave. Just show me the way His father pulled him back and forced him into Quranic school, but the seed was planted. Years later, back with his uncle, tired and searching, Charles finally prayed his own prayer. "Lord, I'm really tired of seeking the truth. Just show me the way." A verse he had heard at a Vacation Bible School came back to him, and in November 1981 he gave his life to Jesus. The cost has been real. Charles is a preacher now, displaced by Mali's conflict and facing daily pressure. But he did not go alone. Of his fourteen siblings, most now follow Jesus, and around a hundred Christians gather at his extended family events. One uncle praying over dinner turned a whole family toward Jesus. Your quiet, ordinary faithfulness may be planting more than you know.

title: He found a Bible in a secondhand shop and thought he was the only Christian in Yemen
summary: 🇾🇪Yemen· 2000s
content: Mohammad grew up in Yemen, in a conservative Muslim home, in a country with almost no visible church at all. About seventeen years ago he found a Bible in a secondhand shop. He took it home and read it in hiding, because being caught with it could cost him everything. What he read pulled him in, and he gave his life to Jesus. Then came a strange loneliness. "When I came to faith, I thought I was the only believer in Yemen," he said. "For a long time, I didn't know any other Yemeni Christians." He was never actually alone He was wrong about being alone, and God kept proving it. Mohammad and his wife Alima, who came to Jesus after reading the Gospels herself, had been unable to have children for seven years. They prayed, and the infertility ended. Once, in a car accident, Mohammad says he saw a white light in the shape of a cross. Slowly he found other Yemeni believers, received discipleship, and today helps lead a house church in one of the hardest places on earth to follow Jesus. The man who thought he was the only one is now helping build a family of them. If you feel like the only believer in your world, take heart. Jesus is already gathering people you have not met yet, and He has not left you on your own.

title: A widow heard the good news from a travelling salesman and could not unhear it
summary: Laos· 2022
content: Pei was a fifty-two-year-old widow in Laos, raised the way her whole village was raised, worshipping ancestors and local spirits in a place where the government pushes atheism and neighbours warn that following the God of foreigners will offend the gods of home. Then a salesman came through and, somewhere between selling his goods, told her about Jesus. Salvation as a gift, not a payment. Pei believed it. She let go of the ancestor worship she had carried her whole life and quietly followed Jesus instead. The cost at her own front door She was discipled in secret for four months, growing strong enough to speak. The first people she told were her daughter and her son-in-law, who happens to be a policeman. They did not celebrate. He threatened her, saying that if she did not stop believing in Jesus, they would report her, jail her, or throw her out. In June they made good on it, tossing her clothes into the yard and telling her to go live with the people who gave her this Jesus. She went. She did not go back. A widow with nothing chose Jesus over a roof, because she had found something no one could evict from her heart. Following Jesus is not always safe, but it is always worth it. What Pei found is worth more than what it cost her, and it is offered to you too.

title: After his daughter was killed, he prayed for a Bible no one could take from him
summary: Uzbekistan and Tajikistan· 2020s
content: Rashid Kadirov was a Muslim in Central Asia when the worst thing happened. His six-year-old daughter Azizza was killed by a drunk neighbour driving a tractor. In his grief he went looking for something the ache could rest on, and he went to the Koran. There he read a line, in Surah 5:70, that pointed back to the Gospels as holy scripture. So he prayed a strange, specific prayer. He asked God for an Injil, a New Testament. His friends brought him one. It was a stolen Gideon Bible, taken from a vandalised car. It did not last. When the friends took it back, Rashid prayed again, this time for a Bible no one could take away from him. The book that stayed Then a couple arrived from Tajikistan, sent by a former classmate of his who had himself come to Christ. They carried a Bible and a copy of the JESUS Film. Rashid and his wife Aleka watched it, and as the good news was explained, each of them, without telling the other, quietly prayed to receive Jesus. Aleka barely understood it all. "She had very little understanding of the Gospel," she said later, "and yet peace flooded her heart." They were baptised in Tajikistan, and Rashid started telling others what he had found. A grieving father asked for a book, and God gave him a Person. The peace Rashid could not manufacture arrived the moment Jesus did. He is close to the brokenhearted, and He is near to you.

title: 35 priests could not help her. In a church she saw Jesus crush what was choking her
summary: 🇱🇰North Central Province· 2021
content: Chandra lived in a rural village in Sri Lanka's North Central Province, and she was slowly falling apart. Pain, weakness, a heart that raced for no reason doctors could name. She and her family were Hindu, so they did what they knew to do. They went to priest after priest. Thirty-five of them. Nothing changed. In July 2021 they walked into a church instead. As people prayed for her, Chandra saw something. Demons were trying to strangle her, and then Jesus Christ stepped in and stamped on them. She felt the pain and the sickness drain out of her body as they were defeated. In the vision Jesus spoke Scripture over her, from Psalm 34. "They looked to Him and were radiant," He said, and told her she would be radiant too if she trusted Him. The prayer a father prayed Her husband Dinesh, a day labourer, watched his wife come back to life and made God a promise. "God, if you will heal my wife, I will dedicate my daughter for your service." The whole family, who had barely heard the name of Jesus, gave their lives to Him. Their daughter Tenusha told her class what had happened, that her mother was free and that Jesus forgives sinners and makes them new. They did not keep it to themselves. A house church started in their home with four people. By now it is forty-six. Jesus is still stronger than whatever is choking the life out of you. He steps in, He stamps it down, and He calls you radiant.

title: He prayed for his mother's infected leg. Then his Muslim neighbours started coming
summary: 🇸🇩El Hasahisa· 2022
content: Pastor Abdalla Haron Sulieman gathered his small church in El Hasahisa, Sudan, to pray for his mother. Aisha Adam was sixty, and a leg infection had worn her down. They prayed, and she recovered. What looked like a private family mercy did not stay private for long. Word of the healing moved through the town, which is mostly Muslim. And people started showing up at the church. Not to argue. To ask if the God who healed Aisha might heal them too. When a healing becomes a door That is exactly the kind of thing that makes some people afraid. Local extremists pressed the police to arrest Sulieman, and they did, charging him under an old law with claiming to be a witch doctor, as if the love of Jesus were a kind of sorcery. Believers across Sudan shared his name and called for his release. "This is a serious violation against Christians in Sudan," said one, an evangelist named Francis Ismail. But notice what the fear could not undo. A mother was well. A Muslim town had seen the name of Jesus do something real, and neighbours who had never entered a church walked in looking for Him. God still heals, and He still uses one ordinary answered prayer to open a door no one can shut. He can open one where you are too.

title: Karma said he had to earn heaven. At 17 he heard he could be forgiven
summary: Rakiraki· 1990s
content: Simon Gounder was born into a strict Hindu family in Fiji. His great-grandfather had been shipped from India as a contract labourer after the British took the islands in 1874, and the family settled in a small village in the north of Viti Levu. Simon grew up inside a system with clear rules. "As a Hindu, we believed in karma," he said. "If you do good karma, you get to heaven. If you do bad karma, you will be punished." It was a ledger he could never quite balance. He knew his own wrongs too well. The night the ledger closed At seventeen, a friend invited him to a Christian youth meeting in another town. There he heard something that did not fit anything he had been taught. That Jesus Christ could simply forgive sins. Not offset them, not average them out over lifetimes. Forgive them. Simon felt the weight of his own failures and, for the first time, an offer to be free of them. "I gave my life to Jesus that night," he said. He hid it from his parents at first. When they found out, they were not happy. But the son who came home changed did not stop there. In time he led his whole family to Christ, and he went on to plant a ministry that carries the same forgiveness to others. Karma keeps a running tab you can never clear. Jesus tears the tab up. Whatever you are carrying tonight, He is still in the business of forgiving it all at once.

title: You can kill me, but you cannot take my faith in Jesus
summary: 🇧🇩Bangladesh· 2021-2022
content: Nur Alam and Afzal Hosen left Islam to follow Jesus in 2021, and they were baptised soon after. They did not keep it quiet. They wanted the Muslim community they came from to know the Jesus they had found, so they handed out Bibles and booklets around their part of Bangladesh. That is when the trouble started. A group seized Nur and locked him in a room for thirty hours, no food, no water, no sleep, demanding he return to Islam and threatening to kill him and his family. He would not bend. "At some point during the interrogation," Nur said, "they became hopeless, seeing my strong faith in Jesus." A faith they could not confiscate Days after Nur was freed, they came for Afzal. They beat him and accused him of being paid to convert. His answer has the ring of the early church about it. "You can kill me," he told them, "but you cannot take my faith in the Lord Jesus away from me." Both men were released, bruised and exhausted and still standing. They had discovered the thing every threat runs into eventually. You can take a man's freedom, his comfort, even his life, but the faith Jesus plants in a heart is not yours to seize. If Jesus is worth that to two young men in Bangladesh, He is worth your whole life too.

title: A soldier who should have died in battle walked into a demon's shrine
summary: 🇲🇲Myanmar· 2010s
content: Pastor Dano was a soldier before he was a pastor. He came out of the battlefield alive when he had no reason to, and he never shook the sense of why. "I believe God preserved my life from death on the battlefield for a purpose," he said. The purpose showed up in a Buddhist village that wanted nothing to do with him. The vice chief's son was tormented, demon-possessed, and no one could help. Dano fasted and prayed for three days. Then, near midnight, he went to the shrine where the boy was and did the only thing he knew to do. "I called upon the name of the Lord," he said, "and the demon left the young man." The night the shrines fell silent Villagers said every evil spirit left the village at once. Dano went from shrine to shrine, praying against the darkness that had ruled the place for generations. The vice chief's family, who had braced for his anger, found grace instead. They gave their lives to Jesus, and four more families followed. The people who once opposed him now follow his lead. There is a church in that village today where there used to be shrines. The name of Jesus is still stronger than every dark thing that has ever frightened you. One believer, praying at midnight, was enough to set a whole village free.

title: They locked the pastor in a psychiatric ward. He led a hundred men to Jesus
content: Pastor Bakhytzhan Kashkumbaev was an elderly man when Kazakhstan arrested him in May 2013. The charges were strange, that he had harmed a church member's health and stirred up religious hatred. They sentenced him toward ten years and put him in a psychiatric ward, where inmates were routinely drugged. On the way in, he thought it might be the end of his mind. "This is probably the last time I will talk to you in my right mind," he said. Then a question reached him, the kind God uses. "Where is your faith?" Under the cover of the risen Lord Something lifted. "I felt like I was under the cover of the risen Lord," he said. The old man who expected to lose himself instead found Jesus nearer than the walls. He started talking to the men around him. To a prisoner wrecked by drug addiction he said simply, "Only Jesus can help you." Over nine months inside, nearly one hundred inmates gave their lives to Christ. "In prison," he said, "the Holy Spirit opened one dimension of prayer to me." The place meant to break him became the most fruitful pulpit of his life. They released him in early 2014. He walked out having planted the good news in the last place anyone would look for it. God is not locked out by any door that locks you in. He was already inside, waiting.

title: Her church offering came to the exact amount of her power bill, to the penny
summary: 🇺🇸United States· 2020s
content: Lina Johnson did not have enough to cover her power bill. She had told no one the amount. Not a friend, not her church, no one. It was her private worry, the kind you carry quietly and hope somehow resolves. That same week an offering came around at church for a family in need, and Lina gave what she could. Twenty-six cents. It was almost nothing, and she gave it anyway. Down to the penny The next day a friend told her the rest of the story. The offering the church had taken was for her. And when they counted it, it came to the exact amount of her power bill. To the penny. "The offering they took in church yesterday was for me," Lina said, "and it was the exact amount as my power bill. It was to the penny and I never told anyone how much my bill was." Here is the detail that undoes you. Had she given more than her twenty-six cents, the total would have overshot the bill, and the provision would have lost its edge. Even her small gift was part of God's arithmetic. God is not rounding up or guessing. He knew the number she never spoke aloud, and He met it precisely, through people who had no idea. The Father who counts the hairs on your head knows your bill too, down to the last penny.

title: He carried a bomb into a church. The sermon was about loving your enemies
summary: 🇮🇩Jakarta· 2000s
content: Ahmad Quraisy was a commanding officer in a militant Islamist group in Indonesia. The economic collapse of the late 1990s had radicalised him, and he blamed Christians for what had gone wrong. So he built a plan. He carried a time bomb into a Protestant church in Jakarta, intending to kill everyone inside. Then he heard the pastor preach. The man was telling his congregation to love their enemies and to pray for the people who persecuted them. Quraisy froze. "I never saw that Christian love before in my life," he said. He could not do it. He carried the bomb back out. His own leaders locked him up for a month for failing. The love he could not detonate That was only the beginning. In the year that followed, Quraisy began having visions he was sure came from Jesus. He was healed of typhus. His wife, unknown to him, had been quietly praying. By 2001 he gave his life to Christ. The man who wanted to blow up a church now builds them. Quraisy leads an underground network of around seven thousand former Muslims meeting in house churches across Indonesia, most of them still keeping a low profile to stay safe. The love that stopped his hand in that church is the same love reaching for you. It is stronger than the worst thing you ever planned to do.

Pour Vianney et son épouse, la violoncelliste Catherine Robert, les prénoms de leurs enfants ont chacun leur petite histoire. Dans une vidéo publiée ce 11 novembre sur Instagram par les comptes Instagram Appellemoirino et Zeniomag, le chanteur s’est confié avec tendresse sur ces choix au micro de l’émission Le Grand Studio Bel RTL. Pour leur premier enfant ensemble, Edgar, aujourd’hui âgé de 5
summary_zh: 有些名字一听就让人心动，有些名字则最终征服了父母的心。对于维亚内和他的妻子、大提琴家凯瑟琳·罗伯特来说，他们孩子的名字都有着各自的小故事。在 Instagram 账户 Appellemoirino 和 Zeniomag 于 11 月 11 日发布的视频中，这位歌手在《Le Grand Studio Bel RTL》节目的麦克风前深情地谈论了这些名字的选择。对于他们的……

content: Il y a les prénoms qui séduisent immédiatement et ceux qui finissent par conquérir le cœur des parents. Pour Vianney et son épouse, la violoncelliste Catherine Robert, les prénoms de leurs enfants ont chacun leur petite histoire. Dans une vidéo publiée ce 11 novembre sur Instagram par les comptes Instagram Appellemoirino et Zeniomag, le chanteur s’est confié avec tendresse sur ces choix au micro de l’émission Le Grand Studio Bel RTL. Pour leur premier enfant ensemble, Edgar, aujourd’hui âgé de 5 ans, le choix s’est imposé presque naturellement. Catherine Robert, déjà maman d’une petite fille née d’une précédente union, et Vianney se sont rapidement accordés, sans même connaître le sexe du bébé à venir. « C’était notre évidence », confie le chanteur. Pour leur petite dernière, Rita, née il y a quelques semaines, l’histoire a été un peu différente. Contrairement à Edgar, le prénom n’a pas immédiatement séduit le chanteur. « Je le trouvais horrible », reconnaît-il avec amusement. Néanmoins, un dîner avec son Tout lire… The post « En termes de sens, c’était très fort »: Vianney raconte le choix des prénoms de ses enfants appeared first on Aleteia .

title: Introducing Father Martin Kilonzo , Parochial Vicar , St . Joseph Catholic Church
summary: My name is Fr. Martin Kilonzo, ALCP/OSS. I am a Roman Catholic priest and a member of the Apostolic Life Community of Priests in Opus Spiritus Sancti (ALCP/OSS). Originally from Kenya, East Africa, I
content: My name is Fr. Martin Kilonzo, ALCP/OSS. I am a Roman Catholic priest and a member of the Apostolic Life Community of Priests in Opus Spiritus Sancti (ALCP/OSS). Originally from Kenya, East Africa, I currently serve as parochial vicar at St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, N.D. My journey has been a remarkable experience of faith, formation, missionary service, and trust in God’s providence. I was born in 1978 in Kilenge, a small village in Makueni County, southeastern Kenya, where I attended elementary school. I later joined Pope Paul VI Minor Seminary in the Diocese of Machakos, my home diocese, where I received a high school education and spiritual formation that helped prepare me for the priesthood. After four years at the minor seminary, I pursued three years of philosophical studies at the Spiritan Missionary Seminary in Arusha, Tanzania, followed by four years of theological studies at Jordan University College in Morogoro, Tanzania. I was ordained a priest in July 2012 in the Diocese of Moshi, in Tanzania’s Kilimanjaro Region. Since my ordination, I have served in various pastoral assignments in Tanzania and Italy, enriching my missionary experience and understanding of different cultures. In 2026, following consultations between my religious superiors and the Bishop of Fargo, I was assigned to the Diocese of Fargo, N.D., beginning a new chapter in my priestly ministry. October 15 holds special significance for me as the anniversary of the day I first set foot on American soil. I arrived in Chicago before taking a connecting flight to Minot, N.D. After spending approximately one week serving at St. Mary’s Cathedral in Fargo, I was assigned to St. Joseph’s Church in Devils Lake, where I officially began my ministry as parochial vicar in February 2026. I consider my assignment in North Dakota a privilege and a renewed call to missionary service. Through God’s grace, I am grateful for the opportunity to celebrate the sacraments, provide spiritual guidance, and serve the parishioners of St. Joseph’s Church and the wider Devils Lake community, regardless of religious affiliation or background. For me, the journey from Kilenge, Kenya, to Devils Lake, N.D., is more than a change of place; it is a continuing response to God’s call to faith, service, and missionary discipleship with humility.

title: Un progetto giovane per la Chiesa missionaria : Wecare .
summary: Un progetto giovane per la Chiesa missionaria: Wecare. Lasciare per alcune settimane la propria casa e le proprie “zone di conforto”, avventurarsi in un altro Paese e condividere tempo e lavoro con pe
content: Un progetto giovane per la Chiesa missionaria: Wecare. Lasciare per alcune settimane la propria casa e le proprie “zone di conforto”, avventurarsi in un altro Paese e condividere tempo e lavoro con persone la cui vita è molto diversa. Per alcuni giovani, le vacanze possono trasformarsi in un’esperienza di incontri e di prossimità con realtà lontane. Dove, riferisce l’agenzia missionaria vaticana Fides, tutto può diventare occasione per interrogarsi su se stessi, sugli altri e sui desideri del proprio cuore. È quanto accade spesso nelle esperienze missionarie promosse da “Wecare”, una realtà italiana le cui radici risalgono a vent’anni fa e che ogni anno coinvolge numerosi giovani in progetti in Italia e in altri Paesi. La storia è iniziata nel 2005, quando Fernando Lozada Baldoceda, iniziatore delle esperienze di volontariato all’estero e oggi direttore di Wecare, organizzò un primo viaggio in Perù con tre universitari. “È stato il primo tentativo di un viaggio di volontariato”, ricorda. Nel 2006 l’esperienza ha iniziato a strutturarsi come gruppo e, negli anni successivi, è cresciuta fino a coinvolgere decine di giovani. Nel 2011 è stata creata una struttura giuridica per sostenere il progetto e, dopo diverse tappe e l’ampliamento delle attività anche in Italia, nel 2023 è nata Wecare nella forma che ha oggi. Per Fernando, più che l’evoluzione di un’organizzazione, questi vent’anni raccontano la storia di giovani che hanno scoperto di avere un tesoro da condividere, e hanno scelto di mettersi in gioco. Chiesa giovane “C’è molta più gioia nel dare che nel ricevere”, racconta Camilla di Roma a Fides. Dopo aver partecipato a un’esperienza in Argentina nel 2025 ha deciso di partire nuovamente quest’anno, questa volta per il Brasile. “Ho scelto di partecipare una seconda volta perché questa esperienza non aiuta soltanto gli altri, aiuta anche me- spiega-. Il contatto con gli altri permette di toccare corde di te che nella vita quotidiana non tocchi e di conoscersi in modo diverso”. In Brasile, uno degli incontri che più l’ha segnata è stato quello con la comunità di Milan dos Coelhos. “Ciò che mi ha colpito di più è stato l’amore che circondava la comunità”, ricorda. In particolare, l’ha colpita il modo in cui le persone si prendevano cura di Evinho, un anziano della comunità. Questo le ha fatto scoprire che, pur avendo molto poco, non mancava loro quello che per lei è il valore più importante: “L’amore per il prossimo, la prossimità e l’aiuto gratuito”. Al ritorno, quell’esperienza aveva cambiato anche il suo modo di guardare alla propria vita. “Sono tornata con una maggiore consapevolezza e con più voglia di aiutare gli altri- evidenzia-. L’esperienza ha ridimensionato le mie priorità e mi ha fatto comprendere meglio ciò per cui vale la pena lottare. Mi sento anche più grata per quello che ho e per ciò che mi circonda”. Anche Benedetta ha scelto di ripartire. Dopo il Perù nel 2022 e il Camerun nel 2025, quest’anno è tornata in Brasile. La frase “C’è più gioia nel dare che nel ricevere” ha accompagnato le sue esperienze. “Mi sento fortunata, ricevo molto ogni giorno e volevo capire che cosa significa davvero dare”, osserva.

title: La Nación / La diócesis de San Lorenzo cuenta con nuevo obispo
summary: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólic
content: El papa León XIV nombró a monseñor Pierre Jubinville como nuevo obispo de la diócesis de San Lorenzo en reemplazo de monseñor Joaquín Robledo, quien presentó renuncia al cargo. La Nunciatura Apostólica en Paraguay comunicó el sábado 7 de noviembre que el santo padre aceptó la renuncia de Robledo y designó en su reemplazo a monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville, quien se desempeñaba como obispo de San Pedro y es el actual presidente de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya (CEP). La decisión fue anunciada por la CEP, conforme a lo establecido en el Código de Derecho Canónico, que contempla la renuncia de los obispos al alcanzar los 75 años de edad. No obstante, monseñor Robledo continuará al frente de la diócesis como administrador apostólico hasta la toma de posesión canónica de su sucesor. La Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya agradeció a monseñor Robledo por su servicio pastoral y dedicación a la Iglesia, al tiempo que encomendó en oración al nuevo obispo, deseándole un fecundo ministerio episcopal en su nueva misión. El nuevo obispo Monseñor Pierre Laurent Jubinville nació el 5 de agosto de 1960 en Ottawa, Canadá. Tras algunas experiencias laborales, ingresó en la Congregación del Espíritu Santo y estudió Teología en la Universidad de Montreal. Emitió los votos solemnes en 1988 y fue ordenado presbítero el 17 de setiembre de 1988. Tras algunas experiencias misioneras en África, realizó estudios académicos en Montreal y París. Llegó a Paraguay en 1991, desarrolló diversas tareas pastorales y formativas; entre ellas, se desempeñó en la pastoral indígena de la parroquia San José Obrero, en la Diócesis de San Pedro; fue párroco de San Francisco de Asís y formador de la Congregación del Espíritu Santo en Asunción. En 2013 fue nombrado obispo de San Pedro y recibió la ordenación episcopal el 21 de diciembre de ese mismo año. Además, ejerció la vicepresidencia de la Conferencia Episcopal Paraguaya entre 2018 y 2024 y, desde noviembre de 2024, ocupa la presidencia de dicha institución. La Diócesis de San Lorenzo comprende varias localidades del departamento Central, entre ellas Capiatá, San Lorenzo, Ñemby, Itá, Ypané, Guarambaré, Villeta, Nueva Italia, San Antonio, J. Augusto Saldívar, Ypacaraí y Thompson.

title: En 2023 , Francisco organizó su sucesión : Puso a Prevost en el lugar idóneo por si soplaba el Espíritu Santo en esa dirección …
summary: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que termi
content: Antes de escribir la biografía de Jorge Bergoglio, que llamó El gran Reformador, Austen Ivereigh ya era un experto en la historia de la Iglesia argentina. “Mi tesis de doctorado [en Oxford], que terminé en el 92, fue sobre catolicismo y política en la Argentina”. Y hay más: “Debo mi fe a la Iglesia Argentina, leyendo artículos de monseñor (Gustavo) Franceschi, volví a la fe”, dice. Ese conocimiento de nuestro país y de su fe mayoritaria representó una ventaja a la hora de escribir sobre Bergoglio, ya que cada etapa de la trayectoria del futuro Papa está debidamente contextualizada en la época que atravesaba el país. Desde aquel marzo de 2013, cuando la novedad de un pontífice argentino y jesuita impactó al mundo entero, Ivereihg siempre pensó que vendría cuando Francisco visitara la Argentina, viaje que finalmente no se concretó. “Ahora vengo con León”, comenta. En efecto, este escritor, historiador, periodista y analista de asuntos religiosos y políticos estará en nuestro país contemporáneamente con la visita del papa León XIV, invitado por la Universidad del Salvador (USAL), donde dictó, el pasado viernes 6, una clase magistral sobre “El giro latinoamericano Francisco-León: la Iglesia misionera sinodal y el cambio de época”. Ivereigh también es co-autor de Let Us Dream (Soñemos Juntos, 2020), un libro escrito en colaboración con Francisco. Su trabajo más reciente es First Belong to God: On Retreat with Pope Francis (Lo primero es pertenecer a Dios: Un retiro con el Papa Francisco, 2024), basado en los escritos y charlas de Bergoglio como director espiritual de un retiro ignaciano de 8 días. De 2004 a 2006, Ivereigh fue colaborador del entonces arzobispo de Westminster, cardenal Cormac Murphy-O’Connor, uno de los más activos promotores de la candidatura de Jorge Mario Bergoglio al papado. Ivereigh considera que el papado de Francisco inició un giro latinoamericano hacia una iglesia misionera y sinodal, cuyo primer paso fue la exhortación apostólica Evangelii Gaudium (noviembre de 2013), sobre “el anuncio del Evangelio en el mundo actual”, con la cual, dice, “Francisco inaugura una hoja de ruta de su Papado que también es la del pontificado de León”. Pero esa hoja de ruta tenía una génesis anterior: el ya famoso documento de Aparecida, la V Conferencia General del Episcopado Latinoamericano y del Caribe (Celam), redactado por Bergoglio. De esta manera, “América Latina pasó a ser la iglesia fuente”, señala, porque “siempre hay una parte de la Iglesia de la cual brota un dinamismo teológico”. Antes, ese rol lo cumplía Europa, pero a partir del Concilio Vaticano II eso cambia porque es en América Latina donde mejor se lo pone en práctica. Aclara que “fuente” no quiere decir centro; de hecho, “Francisco quería una Iglesia multipolar”. — ¿Hasta qué punto Aparecida refleja a Bergoglio como individualidad y hasta dónde es la Iglesia latinoamericana, que usted define como “fuente”? — El proceso de preparación de esa conferencia general, fue muy sinodal, de mucha consulta, y el papel de Bergoglio en esa conferencia general es muy conocido. Creo que influyó la recepción del Concilio Vaticano II en el Río de La Plata, que tuvo un matiz distinto al resto de América Latina. Tal vez, cuando llegó a Aparecida esa visión sobre la religiosidad popular estaba ya madura. Es decir, una teología de espiritualidad latinoamericana, distinta a anteriores teologías latinoamericanas. Bergoglio tenía muchas cosas que eran de él. Pero también llevaba en su forma de ser y de pensar muchos aportes de la iglesia argentina, la influencia de Lucio Gera y de Rafael Tello y toda esa tradición. — ¿Cómo vio el impacto de su papado en la Argentina? — Creo que una de las razones por las que no vino, sobre todo al principio, fue que tenía horror del triunfalismo. Y sabía que tal vez los argentinos tenían —todos los países lo tienen— una cierta tentación de decir: “El Papa es argentino”. Y si le tenía tanto rechazo al triunfalismo, era porque éste pone a uno en el ce

title: Pope warns of dehumanization caused by AI
summary: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 o
content: Pope Leo XIV waves to faithful from the popemobile upon his arrival for a prayer vigil at the Centenario Stadium in Montevideo on November 7, 2026. (AFP Photo) Pope Leo XIV warned students on Nov. 7 of “dehumanization” through the use of AI in education, and urged schools and university to place the “person before the algorithm.” “The process of dehumanization we are experiencing poses a challenge,” the pope, who has warned repeatedly about the need to ensure AI is used ethically, said in a speech at the Catholic University of Uruguay. Just three weeks after undergoing surgery for lung cancer, the 71-year-old pontiff is on a 12-day tour of South Africa where he served nearly two decades as a missionary. On Nov. 7, he visited the crime-blighted Montevideo neighborhood of Casavalle. The murder rate in the impoverished district is four times the national average and residents spoke movingly of the dangers they faced, like commonplace gun violence. Katherine Silva’s voice cracked with emotion as she told the pope about the violence and abuse she had suffered as a child. After ending up homeless at 15, the young mother said she “went through very dark times” and “nearly died.” “There are children in Uruguay who do not go to school for fear of never returning home,” Leo said. “In a country as rich in resources as this, children should never have to go to bed hungry... Much less should they have to suffer violence to the point of losing their lives,” he added. As police helicopters flew overhead, locals waved and cheered to welcome the head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics, who blessed 12 new low-income houses financed by the Church.

title: Il Mimmo Beneventano a padre Zanotelli , Leo Amato e alla memoria di Massimo Battista - Notizie
summary: Saranno assegnati a padre Alex Zanotelli, al giornalista Leo Amato e alla memoria di Massimo Battista (consigliere comunale di Taranto, operaio dell'ex Ilva e attivista) i riconoscimenti dell'edizione
content: Saranno assegnati a padre Alex Zanotelli, al giornalista Leo Amato e alla memoria di Massimo Battista (consigliere comunale di Taranto, operaio dell'ex Ilva e attivista) i riconoscimenti dell'edizione 2026 del 'Riconoscimento Nazionale Mimmo Beneventano', la cui cerimonia di premiazione è in programma sabato prossimo, 14 novembre, a Sasso di Castalda (Potenza). Ne ha dato notizia Libera Basilicata, ricordando che "il 7 novembre è una data che porta con sé una ferita ancora aperta, ma anche una testimonianza che il tempo non ha cancellato. In questo giorno del 1980, a Ottaviano, veniva assassinato dalla camorra Mimmo Beneventano, giovane medico, consigliere comunale e uomo impegnato nella difesa della propria comunità dalle infiltrazioni e dalle speculazioni della criminalità organizzata. Beneventano - è ricordato nel comunicato - aveva scelto di non voltarsi dall'altra parte, opponendosi apertamente agli interessi della Nuova Camorra Organizzata e pagando con la vita il proprio impegno. A distanza di 46 anni, il suo esempio continua a rappresentare un riferimento per quanti credono nella democrazia, nella libertà, nella giustizia sociale e nella necessità di contrastare ogni forma di sopraffazione mafiosa. È proprio nel segno di questa eredità civile e morale che sabato 14 novembre, a Sasso di Castalda, paese caro a Mimmo per le origini familiari e nel cui cimitero riposa, si terrà il XVIII Riconoscimento Nazionale Mimmo Beneventano, appuntamento annuale dedicato a valorizzare l'impegno di donne e uomini che, attraverso il proprio lavoro e le proprie scelte, contribuiscono ad affermare i valori della democrazia e della legalità contro le mafie e la corruzione". Per l'edizione 2026 "i riconoscimenti saranno assegnati a tre personalità provenienti da ambiti diversi, ma accomunate da percorsi di impegno civile e professionale. Padre Alex Zanotelli, missionario comboniano e giornalista, è una figura di riferimento nel panorama dell'impegno sociale e della cooperazione internazionale. Per anni ha vissuto a Korogocho, una delle baraccopoli di Nairobi, condividendo la quotidianità delle comunità più povere. È stato direttore della rivista Nigrizia e successivamente di Mosaico di pace, distinguendosi per la sua attività di denuncia e per le battaglie sui temi della pace, del disarmo, della giustizia sociale e dell'acqua come bene comune. Massimo Battista, al quale il riconoscimento sarà conferito alla memoria, è stato consigliere comunale di Taranto, operaio dell'ex Ilva e attivista. Ha legato il proprio percorso personale e pubblico alle vicende della città di Taranto, impegnandosi nelle questioni riguardanti il mondo del lavoro, la salute dei cittadini e la tutela ambientale. La sua figura resta legata alle battaglie civili e sociali del territorio tarantino. Leo Amato, giornalista, ha svolto una parte significativa della propria attività professionale in Basilicata, collaborando con Il Quotidiano del Sud, per poi proseguire il suo percorso anche a livello nazionale nella redazione de Il Fatto Quotidiano. Nel corso della sua carriera si è occupato di cronaca, politica e inchieste, seguendo da vicino vicende e questioni di interesse pubblico legate ai territori. Tre storie e tre percorsi che saranno al centro della cerimonia di quest'anno, nel solco dei valori che hanno contraddistinto la vita di Mimmo Beneventano". Riproduzione riservata © Copyright ANSA

title: Kehilangan yang Membawa Berkah
title_zh: 带来祝福的失去
content: Oleh: Gevonny Dinda Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Gevonny Dinda, biasa dipanggil Dinda. Sebagai orang Kristen, saya merasa bersyukur dilahirkan di dunia ini dan berkesempatan untuk mengenal Tuhan Yesus. Saya sungguh bahagia dapat merasakan berkat-Nya setiap hari dan sangat bersyukur akan apa yang Tuhan Yesus berikan kepada saya selama ini. Kabar baik, kabar buruk, cobaan, dan berkat, saya terima dengan penuh rasa ucapan syukur. Di sini, saya akan menceritakan salah satu berkat Tuhan dalam kehidupan saya. Pada 19 Februari 2015, saya menerima kabar buruk bahwa kakek saya telah berpulang ke rumah Tuhan. Kepergian kakek saya sangat membekas di hati banyak orang, terutama nenek saya. Nenek saya sangat merasa kehilangan karena memang nenek belum siap menghadapi hal ini sehingga membuat kondisi badannya melemah. Sejak ditinggal kakek, kondisi mental dan fisik nenek saya semakin memburuk. Awalnya, ia merasa sangat kesepian dan merasa takut jika ditinggal sendirian di rumah. Bahkan, nenek saya sering menangis jika merasa kesepian. Ibu saya dan ketujuh saudara kandungnya akhirnya sepakat untuk bergantian menjaga nenek saya di rumahnya supaya tidak merasa kesepian lagi. Setelah itu, hari-hari nenek saya berjalan normal seperti biasa. Namun, karena umurnya yang bertambah tua, kondisi fisiknya semakin melemah. Sejak 2017, nenek saya sudah tidak kuat lagi berjalan dan harus memakai kursi roda. Di situlah, ketabahan dan kesabaran anak-anaknya, termasuk ibu saya, diuji dalam mengurus nenek saya. Pakde, budhe, tante, dan om saya yang hidup di luar kota, seperti: Jakarta, Yogyakarta, dan Kudus, semakin sering menyempatkan diri pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bergiliran mengurus nenek saya. Sampai pada April 2018 lalu, kondisi nenek saya berada di titik terburuknya. Karena anak-anaknya sudah memiliki firasat yang tidak baik, mereka memutuskan untuk berkunjung bersama-sama ke rumah nenek saya. Mereka hanya bisa berdoa bersama untuk kondisi ibu mereka. Sampai pada akhirnya, Tuhan Yesus memanggil nenek saya untuk ikut bersama-Nya. Karena sudah siap dengan kepergian nenek saya, kami semua menerima kepergian nenek dengan sukacita dan penuh ucapan syukur karena nenek saya sudah sembuh dan pergi ke tempat yang lebih indah, menyusul kakek saya. Tidak disangka, kepergian kakek dan nenek saya membawa berkah bagi keluarga besar kami. Tuhan Yesus memiliki kuasa untuk membuat keluarga kami menjadi lebih dekat satu sama lain. Hubungan anak-anak beserta cucu-cucu mereka menjadi lebih dekat. Kakak-kakak Ibu saya yang dahulu sering pulang ke Salatiga hanya untuk bertemu dan menjenguk orang tua mereka, sekarang lebih menghargai waktu kebersamaan dengan keluarga yang diberikan oleh Tuhan. Sejak saat itu, kami semua memiliki satu grup chat dan sering menanyakan kabar satu sama lain. Bahkan, kami semua memiliki keinginan untuk lebih sering bertemu pada masa depan, dan melakukan kegiatan bersama-sama seperti berlibur dan arisan keluarga. Semua itu tidak pernah terjadi sebelum kepergian kakek dan nenek saya, dan saya sungguh percaya Tuhan Yesus turut campur tangan dalam semua kejadian yang menimpa keluarga saya. Ia tidak pernah berhenti untuk menunjukkan betapa sayangnya Ia terhadap anak-anak-Nya, bahkan ketika anak-anak-Nya sedang berada dalam keterpurukan. Tuhan Yesus selalu memiliki rencana yang indah untuk setiap anak-anak-Nya, dan saya sangat percaya Ia telah memberikan sesuatu yang besar untuk membalas rasa kehilangan keluarga saya selama ini. Tuhan Yesus memang sungguh baik! Semoga Tuhan selalu memberkati keluarga Anda!

title: Berbagi dengan Mengajar dan Melayani
title_zh: 通过教学和侍奉来分享
content: Shalom! Perkenalkan nama saya Zefanya. Saya bersyukur karena pada kesempatan ini, saya dapat menyaksikan cinta kasih Tuhan yang Ia nyatakan melalui kegiatan mengajar bahasa Inggris yang saya lakukan secara volunter untuk anak-anak di beberapa desa di sekitar kota Salatiga. Kegiatan yang diselenggarakan oleh salah satu yayasan Kristen yang bergerak di bidang pelayanan dan pendidikan ini dilakukan setiap hari minggu. Pada kesempatan itu, saya beserta teman kuliah dan satu staf dari yayasan mendapat tugas untuk mengajar anak-anak di sebuah desa yang letaknya cukup jauh dari kota Salatiga, tempat kami tinggal. Butuh waktu sekitar dua jam lebih untuk sampai ke sana. Selama perjalanan, medan yang dilalui cukup sulit karena kami harus melewati jalanan aspal yang telah rusak parah dan jalanan tanah yang cukup sempit. Kami juga harus bersahabat dengan hawa panas yang sangat menyengat akibat dari teriknya sinar matahari ditambah dengan banyaknya tanah tandus dan pohon kering di sepanjang perjalanan. Namun, hal tersebut tidak mengurangi semangat kami untuk bertemu dengan anak-anak yang akan kami ajar. Setelah melalui perjalanan yang cukup melelahkan, akhirnya kami tiba di salah satu rumah warga yang akan kami gunakan untuk kegiatan belajar mengajar. Beberapa anak telah berkumpul di dalam rumah itu dan ketika mereka melihat kedatangan kami, mereka langsung membentuk barisan memanjang dan satu per satu mulai memberikan salam kepada kami. Alangkah manisnya! Saya sangat kagum dengan sikap mereka yang sangat ramah yang dapat membuat siapa saja ingin tersenyum ketika melihat mereka. Saya mulai mengajak mereka bercerita tentang pelajaran mereka di sekolah. Ada sekitar dua puluh anak yang datang untuk belajar. Usia mereka bervariasi, dari usia TK hingga SMP. Melalui percakapan mereka, saya mengetahui bahwa sebagian besar dari mereka belum pernah diajarkan bahasa Inggris di sekolah. Anak-anak SMP pun belum mengetahui pelajaran bahasa Inggris tingkat dasar seperti berhitung dari satu hingga sepuluh, atau menulis kosakata sederhana lainnya. Mereka juga bercerita tentang harapan mereka ke depan untuk memiliki fasilitas belajar yang memadai dan memperoleh lebih banyak kesempatan lagi untuk belajar bahasa Inggris. Hal itulah yang membuat kami sadar betapa mereka sangat ingin belajar hal-hal baru, tetapi fasilitas yang ada masih jauh dari kata memadai. Saya pun bersyukur karena dari kegiatan ini, mereka mendapat kesempatan untuk mempelajari hal-hal baru tersebut. Waktu belajar dimulai. Kami mengawalinya dengan berdoa, dan sebagian besar dari mereka, yang berbeda keyakinan, ikut melipat tangan dan menutup mata mereka. Selesai berdoa, kami membagi mereka dalam kelompok kelas kecil dan kelas besar. Kelas kecil terdiri dari anak usia TK hingga kelas tiga SD, sedangkan kelas besar terdiri dari anak-anak kelas empat SD ke atas. Saya mendapat kesempatan untuk mengajar anak-anak kelas besar. Banyak hal yang saya coba ajarkan kepada mereka, mulai dari kosakata sederhana tentang binatang, mengerjakan soal, hingga bermain gim sederhana untuk mengasah kemampuan bahasa Inggris mereka. Rasa lelah dan capai tentu kami rasakan karena mengajar anak-anak seusia mereka bukanlah perkara yang mudah. Namun, pada saat seperti itulah, kami menyadari bahwa kegiatan tersebut kami lakukan untuk memuliakan nama Tuhan. Kami yakin dan percaya bahwa Tuhanlah yang akan memberi kekuatan yang membuat kami mampu untuk melakukannya dengan baik. Kegiatan hari itupun selesai. Kami bersyukur bahwa kegiatan mengajar itu dapat kami lakukan dengan cukup baik terlepas dari kekurangan dan kendala yang kami rasakan sewaktu mengajar. Semangat belajar dari anak-anak juga membuat kami terdorong untuk memberikan pengajaran yang lebih baik lagi pada masa yang akan datang. Kami sangat bersyukur karena Tuhan memberikan perlindungan dan kasih-Nya kepada anak-anak yang kami ajar sehingga mereka masih dapat bertumbuh dengan baik dan memperoleh kesempatan-kesempatan untuk mengembangkan pengetahuan mereka. K

title: Tuhan Menuntunku Mengenal Pribadi-Nya
title_zh: 神引导我认识祂自己
content: Karena dilahirkan dan dibesarkan dalam keluarga Katolik Roma, saya dididik dengan segala tata cara mereka semenjak kecil. Sejak usia yang sangat muda, saya terbiasa mengakui dosa-dosa saya, dengan teguh percaya bahwa dosa-dosa saya diampuni pada waktu pengakuan dosa. Sering kali, beban dosa saya menjadi begitu besar sehingga setelah pengakuan dosa dan merasa bahwa dosa-dosa saya hilang, saya kemudian berharap untuk segera mati sebelum saya berbuat dosa lagi. Namun, pemikiran ini hanya sebentar karena hal itu hanya berlangsung beberapa menit sebelum saya kemudian berbuat dosa lagi, baik dalam pemikiran maupun tindakan. Pada waktu Paskah, selama pembacaan kisah penderitaan Kristus, semua penderitaan-Nya, dan akhirnya kematian-Nya, terkadang saya berpikir, "Mengapa Dia membiarkan mereka membunuh-Nya? Mengapa Dia tidak menghindar dari situasi itu?" Karena Dia adalah Allah, Dia dapat melakukannya. Namun, saya tidak mendapat jawaban. Sering kali, saya akan berpikir, "Apa yang akan saya katakan kepada Allah ketika saya bertemu Dia dengan semua dosa saya?" Sebagai seorang remaja, beban dosa saya sangat besar dan sangat berat bagi saya. Saya tidak tahu di mana saya akan berada dalam keabadian, dan orang-orang yang saya tanyakan memiliki kebingungan yang sama dengan saya. "Di mana jawabannya? Siapa yang memiliki jawabannya? Agama apa yang benar?" Saya bertanya. Namun, saya tidak pernah meragukan bahwa Gereja Katolik Roma adalah jalan yang benar. Hanya, saya tidak dapat menemukan kedamaian. Setelah saya menikah, keadaannya sama. Kemudian, saya memikirkan Alkitab. Meskipun saya belum pernah melihat ke dalamnya, saya tahu isinya akan benar. Firman Allah akan memiliki jawaban untuk saya, jawaban atas pertanyaan saya. Ke mana saya pergi: ke surga? Ke neraka? Bagaimana saya dapat mengetahuinya? Jika saya menuju surga, baiklah. Akan tetapi, jika saya menuju neraka, apakah ada yang bisa saya lakukan? Dan, selama masa-masa ini, saya menjadi semakin religius. Akhirnya, pada November 1975, saya menyuarakan keinginan saya untuk memiliki Alkitab, untuk membaca sendiri firman Tuhan. Suami saya berjanji untuk membelikan saya Alkitab sebagai hadiah Natal. Pada 8 Desember, dua pria yang dikenal oleh suami saya datang ke rumah kami, berbicara kepada kami tentang Tuhan Yesus Kristus, dan mengatakan bahwa mereka mengetahui dengan pasti bahwa mereka akan pergi ke surga, dan itu adalah menurut Alkitab. Mereka meninggalkan kami dengan sebuah buku Injil Yohanes, menunjukkan kepada kami satu atau dua ayat dari Alkitab, dan kemudian pergi. Salah satu dari ayat-ayat itu adalah "Sesungguhnya Aku mengatakan kepadamu, orang yang mendengar perkataan-Ku dan percaya kepada Dia yang mengutus Aku memiliki hidup kekal, dan tidak masuk ke dalam penghakiman karena ia sudah pindah dari kematian ke kehidupan" (Yohanes 5:24, AYT). Saya memikirkan betapa bahagianya orang-orang itu, yang secara pasti mengetahui tempat mereka akan menghabiskan kekekalan. Tepat seminggu kemudian, pada 15 Desember, pada larut malam, saya duduk dan membaca buku kecil lain yang saya dapatkan, God's Way of Salvation (Jalan Keselamatan Allah - Red.). Saya memahami dari buku tersebut bahwa meskipun keselamatan itu gratis bagi saya dan tidak dapat diperoleh dengan cara apa pun, itu tentu membuat Allah membayar dengan mahal. Dia telah memberikan Anak-Nya yang terkasih untuk mati bagi dosa di salib Kalvari. Namun, saya masih bingung bagaimana cara mendapatkan keselamatan ini. Kemudian, saya memikirkan hal-hal yang saya percayai untuk membawa saya ke surga: Agama saya, saya dorong keluar. Agama tidak dapat membantu saya. Baptisan saya, saya membuangnya.
